PulseChain Safe governance and rollup controls
The copied GnosisDAO Safes and Arbitrum administration show substantial, verified postfork control
changes. The inspected Synthetix protocolDAO and Optimism administrator Safes retain their inherited
public configurations. These findings support a concrete module-based control pathway, but do not
establish one group's control of every Safe, Synthetix council or messenger.
Scope and pinned evidence
All blockchain work was read-only: getters, runtime code, storage, logs, transaction receipts, block
headers and historical traces. No transaction was signed or broadcast, and no administrative action was
simulated.
Current reads use PulseChain chain 369, block 27,685,402, hash 
0x085116030d59ed608fabf0595a92b60a76e766282251553249a4d359c92db59d. Inherited comparisons use Ethereum block
17,232,999, hash 0xe5667f9cafb115b1dcfc36b0b569a5601f01dfa000698140a1298ef4f87e2e37. Postfork event ranges
start at block 17,233,000; rollup role deployment queries also include earlier March 2023 history.
Evidence and gap retries are frozen in artifacts/pulsechain-safe-governance-rollup-20261001/.
What a Safe takeover would actually require
Safe owners normally need the configured signature threshold. An enabled module has a separate
execution route. An oracle-backed module can therefore execute a transaction without assembling the
ordinary owner signatures, provided its own acceptance conditions pass. This is why owner lists alone
are insufficient. The Safe module documentation describes this authority; the deployed module's code
supplies its actual conditions.
Controlling GnosisDAO, SafeDAO or a Zodiac factory does not automatically control unrelated Safes. A
concrete link must exist through an enabled module, owner, delegated role, implementation or
authenticated relay. Casting a governance vote through a Safe does not change its signing configuration.
pDAI stabilization thesis · 4 October 2026 345

Verified GnosisDAO module execution and owner changes
T wo linked Safes matter:
Safe Inherited configuration Configuration at the current pin
GnosisDAO Safe 
0x0da0c3e52c977ed3cbc641ff02dd271c3
ed55afe
3 of 5; Reality module enabled 1 of 6; no enabled modules
Treasury/active-management Safe 
0x849d52316331967b6ff1198e5e32a0eb1
68d039d
3 of 10 1 of 11
On 10 June 2026 at 22:13:15 UTC, transaction 0xcbd5…867d called the copied Reality module 
0x0d70332ceb7f3c94b061cda48327891e3449a9e1. Its historical trace reads the oracle's accepted answer, bond and
finalization state, then calls the Safe through execTransactionFromModule. The Safe adds 
0xa8ed85b1d441da00270ecc6dc3600f3cba9d4a03 and reduces its threshold to one. Receipt-verified AddedOwner, 
ChangedThreshold and ExecutionFromModuleSuccess logs corroborate the trace.
Five and a half minutes later, 0xdfcd…7e93 disabled the Reality module. The new owner was then sufficient
for ordinary Safe execution under the reduced threshold.
On 18 June 2026, 0x9c53…2b37 used the GnosisDAO Safe, which was already an enabled module of the
treasury Safe, to add the same address there and reduce the treasury threshold to one. Its receipt and
six-call trace confirm the nested route.
Later history matters. In September, all five original GnosisDAO owners were removed; the added owner
was replaced by 0x147b0ef96881ba4f8fcc18d50a14f1231f5021f5; the five original owners were then restored.
Consequently, a present-day owner-list comparison conceals intermediate removals. At the pin, each of
six owners can authorize alone. The treasury likewise has 11 eligible owners at threshold one.
Neither Safe is presently exclusive to the newly added address.
The old Reality module's current owner/avatar/target remain the GnosisDAO Safe. Its inherited settings
still specify a two-day question timeout, two-day cooldown, seven-day answer expiration and 100-token
minimum bond. It is currently disabled at that Safe. A separate Zodiac Roles module remains enabled at
the treasury; its four registered members match the inherited snapshot. Zero default roles do not prove
that those members have no explicitly selected role permissions.
This proves changed execution authority and the route that changed it. It does not establish a legitimate
Snapshot vote, malicious intent, stolen keys or common control with the five previously examined
research wallets. Those attribution questions need additional evidence.
Synthetix protocolDAO and Optimism remain separate
The Synthetix owner is the protocolDAO Safe at 0xeb3107117fead7de89cd14d463d340a2e6917769, still 5 of 13,
nonce 2,884, with no enabled modules. The Optimism AddressManager owner is 
0x9ba6e03d8b90de867373db8cf1a58d2f7f006b3a, still 5 of 7, nonce 81, with no enabled modules. The selected
postfork configuration-event census found no changes for either Safe; retries recovered initially
unavailable ranges.
Accepted Reality oracle answer
Enabled Reality module
GnosisDAO Safe: threshold
becomes 1
Treasury Safe: threshold
becomes 1
pDAI stabilization thesis · 4 October 2026 346

One Optimism signer is a nested Safe at 0x42d27eea1ad6e22af6284f609847cb3cd56b9c64, still 2 of 2, nonce 10,
with no enabled modules. Its two owners and public configuration match the inherited state. Controlling
that nested Safe would supply one parent signer, not the five required by the parent.
Inspected singleton/fallback runtime code matches inherited code. Guard/fallback storage was checked;
the legacy Safe 1.1.1 does not implement the later 1.3 guard mechanism. Configuration equality does
not establish who currently holds the private keys.
The council study (Appendix 68) expands this to Treasury, Ambassador, Grants and incentive Safes, the
17/22-seat distinction and the old L1 Spartan NFT. Their copied public controls also match the inherited
comparison. Current private-L2 council membership and the Spartan bond-custody Safe remain
unresolved.
Synthetix's own authenticated owner relay is an independent administration path: protocolDAO can send
messages to suitably owned L2 contracts without controlling the global Optimism messenger. Earlier
verified transactions demonstrate that architecture. They do not prove that permissionless callers
executing an inherited proposal own the messenger.
What the copied Optimism BondManager does
The BondManager is 0xcd626e1328b41fcf24737f137bcd4ce0c32bc8d1. Its locally verified implementation of 
isCollateralized(address) is a stub that returns whether the address equals the AddressManager's 
OVM_Proposer. It contains no functioning deposit-based admission system or elected validator committee.
At the pin, the registered proposer is 0x473300df21d047806a082244b417f96b32f13a33. The BondManager returns
true for that address and false for all five examined research wallets and the zero address. The proposer,
sequencer and selected registry dependencies match inherited values; the selected AddressManager
mapping/ownership event census found no postfork changes.
The StateCommitmentChain's append logic still checks this admission predicate. Its 12,592,000-second
sequencer publishing window does not bypass BondManager authorization. The configured fraud-proof
window is 604,800 seconds: seven days. Depositing funds, electing SNX councillors or controlling an
unrelated Safe does not satisfy this copied proposer check.
SCC/CTC storage containers are registered dependencies whose owner identifiers resolve through the
same AddressManager, rather than independent hidden owner Safes. SCC/CTC counters match the
inherited snapshot. Previously verified postfork withdrawals used inherited April/May 2023 roots; they do
not establish a new privately asserted Optimism state root.
Arbitrum: verified administration transfers and open validator admission
The copied rollup at 0x5ef0d09d1e6204141b4d37530808ed19f60fba35 has the UpgradeExecutor at 
0x3fffbadaf827559da092217e474760e2b2c3cedd as owner. Its normal executor role still includes the L1 timelock 
0xe6841d92b0c345144506576ec13ecf5103ac7f49 and the security-council Safe 
0x3666a60ff589873ced457a9a8a0aa6f83d708767. The security council remains 9 of 12, with inherited owners,
nonce 13 and no enabled modules.
However, normal-role equality omits the upgrade path:
pDAI stabilization thesis · 4 October 2026 347

Verified change Evidence and resulting authority
24 February 2025 0xd358…e6f0 executes through the L1 timelock and
UpgradeExecutor. It reduces the minimum timelock delay
from 259,200 seconds to one second and transfers proxy-
admin ownership to 
0xb8698cfffdaaf26ca21fe8aa560c18cc2b2f5996.
19 June 2026 0x8850…2953 changes the copied Inbox proxy's admin to 
0x63a1c70df12ef3d3de17487179465c021de690f4. The current
admin slot confirms it.
19 July 2026 0x1fb1…aeb5 changes the UpgradeExecutor proxy's admin
itself to 0xb8698cfffdaaf26ca21fe8aa560c18cc2b2f5996.
Current storage and receipt-verified AdminChanged
corroborate the trace.
1 September 2026 0x7d7f…d5cc routes another timelock execution through the
executor and changes multiple proxy admins. The Bridge,
SequencerInbox and ChallengeManager admin slots
now contain 0xa0b347117a878da9942fa5c31b87c773a2969913.
Both emphasized admin addresses have empty code at the pin. This is concrete externally owned
address control of important upgrade paths. It can be more consequential than membership of the
unchanged executor/security-council roles. It does not prove common ownership of all these addresses
or that an upgrade has actually altered the currently inspected implementations. The older bridge
ProxyAdmin's owner has subsequently changed again; its current getter returns 
0x353e1d055ae5352d1b8c9d3f0ffef1e3a4b96294, so the February recipient must not be described as its current
owner.
The timelock's scheduling path authenticates the bridge and registered L2 timelock. Permissionless
execution of a ready operation is not permission to schedule one. The original chain's governance
authority and the copied system's accepted messaging therefore need separate treatment.
The validator whitelist changed from enabled to disabled between adjacent blocks 17,322,437 and
17,322,438, on 21 May 2023. The accepted transaction 0x90ca…272b invokes removeWhitelistAfterFork()
through a helper. The recorded selector matches a separately hashed signature. The deployed user logic
permits this when the chain ID has changed: it is a public fork escape, not proof that its caller held the
rollup admin key. Binary search located this transition; it is not an exhaustive proof that no other
transitions occurred elsewhere.
There are 18 active staker addresses at the pin, compared with two in the inherited snapshot. Several
later admin recipients also occur among those active stakers. This establishes address overlap, not 18
independent operators or exclusive validator control. Although the five original research wallets still
return false from the stored isValidator list, the disabled whitelist removes that list as the admission
barrier. Staking, assertion ancestry, timing and challenge conditions still apply.
Implication for the peg thesis
The evidence now supports a stronger statement: module-based changes occurred in copied
Gnosis governance, and externally owned addresses acquired key copied Arbitrum
administration paths. Those are concrete mechanisms for changing local authority. Across's previously
verified oSnap execution provides another protocol-specific example.
pDAI stabilization thesis · 4 October 2026 348

The evidence still does not show that those routes control the inspected Synthetix protocolDAO or copied
Optimism proposer. Arbitrum admission/upgrade authority, Optimism source-root acceptance, Synthetix
collateralized issuance, destination synth minting and Curve liquidity are distinct dependencies. Bridged
supply must pass the relevant route for the exact destination token. One verified control path does not
supply every missing link.
Reproduction and limits
Getter manifests are Research/experiments/pulsechain_safe_governance_*20261001.json; history manifests include
nested controls and rollup roles. probe_pulsechain_routes.py was always supplied explicit getter manifests. 
collect_pulsechain_events.py records query errors separately from receipt verification. Original failed
records remain preserved; retries close the recorded root Safe, rollup-role and nested Reality query gaps.
pulsechain_safe_governance_followup_20261001.py records missing receipts/headers and exact proxy-admin
storage reads. pulsechain_rollup_admission_boundary_20261001.py records the historical adjacent-block whitelist
comparison. Historical trace_transaction and trace_block results explain execution already recorded on-
chain.
No source RPC was available for the private copied L2. Private-key custody, current private-L2 elections,
Snapshot authorization for the Gnosis execution, the Spartan bond-custody Safe and common-control
attribution remain unverified. These limits are specific remaining evidence requirements, not
assumptions that the proposed architecture is impossible.
pDAI stabilization thesis · 4 October 2026 349
